items.title: Generally Available: Microsoft Defender for Cloud support for Azure Container Apps (Serverless Containers Posture)
items.description:
Customers can now bring Azure Container Apps environments into Microsoft Defender for Cloud’s Serverless Containers Posture experience, helping security teams extend posture management across more of their container estate from a single workflow. This makes it easier to gain visibility into Container Apps resources and assess risks across areas such as identity, networking, and container or image configuration. 

With this capability, teams can more consistently evaluate risk across container environments and use attack path analysis to identify potential exposure faster. The result is a more unified security posture, less manual effort, and stronger confidence when securing Container Apps deployments. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Windows Server 2025 on AKS
items.description:
Organizations running Windows-based workloads on Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) face increasing pressure to modernize as support timelines for older Windows Server versions approach retirement. To help customers prepare, AKS now offers GA support for Windows Server 2025, bringing significant improvements such as Stable ABI, Generation 2 VM default, containerd 2.0, and FIPS enablement by default.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Artifact Streaming on AKS
items.description:
You can now accelerate your containerized workloads on Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) using Azure Container Registry (ACR) with Artifact streaming. Artifact streaming will allow you to scale your workloads without having to fully wait for images to be pulled into the clusters.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Confidential VMs for Azure Linux
items.description:
Confidential Virtual Machines (CVM) offer strong security and confidentiality for tenants. CVM for Azure Linux in AKS is now generally available and enables node pools with CVM to target the migration of highly sensitive container workloads to AKS without any code refactoring while benefiting from the features of AKS. 

You can create new node pools using supported CVM vm sizes with Azure Linux 3. The nodes in a node pool created with CVM use a customized Azure Linux 3 image specially configured for CVM. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Purchase order mapping available in Microsoft Marketplace
items.description:
Align Microsoft Marketplace purchases to your business's accounting needs. Purchase order mapping helps allocate your Microsoft invoice, including Marketplace purchases, making it easier to reconcile your organization's cloud and AI spend. Get supplemental invoice views by purchase order and remap spend for up to three months after invoicing, so your teams get the flexibility to adapt as your needs evolve.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Firewall auto-learn SNAT routes
items.description:
Azure Firewall’s auto-learn SNAT routes is now generally available, automatically learning registered and private destination prefixes periodically and applying them as No-SNAT ranges to preserve original source IPs and simplify SNAT management.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Copilot Observability Agent supports Basic and Auxiliary table plans
items.description:
Azure Copilot Observability Agent, an AI-powered operational companion in Azure Monitor, is now covering Log Analytics data in Basic and Auxiliary table plans during interactive analysis and deep investigations. 

Teams can move high-volume telemetry - including container stdout and stderr, audit trails, and node syslog - to lower-cost table plans while keeping supported data available to the agent alongside metrics, traces, topology, and Azure resource context. 

This is especially useful for Kubernetes operations, where high-volume telemetry such as ContainerLogV2, AKS audit logs, and control-plane logs can be candidates for the Basic table plan. 

If eligible tables already use the Basic or Auxiliary plans, no additional user configuration is required.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Monitor Auxiliary Logs Plan in Azure Government and China regions
items.description:
The Auxiliary table plan in Azure Monitor Logs is a cost-effective option for ingesting and retaining high-volume, verbose logs used for compliance and auditing. Auxiliary Logs is now generally available in the sovereign clouds: Azure Government (Fairfax) and China.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Monitor Auxiliary Logs Plan support for Azure tables and plan switching
items.description:
The Auxiliary table plan in Azure Monitor Logs gives you a cost-effective way to ingest and retain high-volume, verbose logs that you keep for compliance and auditing but rarely query. Two highly requested capabilities are now generally available.

Auxiliary now supports a subset of standard Azure tables, in addition to DCR-based custom tables (_CL). You can keep low-value data on its original standard table — retaining its name, schema, and existing queries — instead of building custom pipelines to reshape it.

You can also switch existing tables between the Analytics and Auxiliary plans without recreating them. The change applies to the table in place, so you keep history, schema, and integrations, and the switch is fully reversible as your workload evolves.

Learn more.
